subject: Liability cap — fee-multiplier vs term-aggregate options
messages:
From: James O'Neil <james.oneil@fikahealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@fikahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Liability cap ask — alignment to fees paid

Aditya,

Appreciate the walkthrough today. Procurement at Fika is proposing that the MSA liability cap be tied directly to fees paid rather than a fixed dollar ceiling. Their preferred language is: the greater of (i) $1.5M or (ii) 3x fees paid in the 12 months prior to claim.

They've attached our redlines with the requested language (see attachment). The rationale: easier internal approval if the exposure scales with spend. Two quick asks from our side:
- Can Redwood accept a fee-linked multiplier (3x) with a rolling 12-month lookback?
- If not, would Redwood consider a term-aggregate approach (e.g., 2x total fees over the contract term)?

We also need clarity on carve-outs: procurement wants consequential damages excluded, but will accept IP indemnity and data-breach carveouts.

Attachment: Fika_Health_Redlines_20270511.docx (docx)

Can we sync tomorrow for 20 min? We need a short position to present to our GC.

Thanks,
James O'Neil
Senior Procurement Manager
Fika Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Liability cap ask — alignment to fees paid

James — thanks and good to meet earlier. Looping in Markus (legal) and Laura (rev ops) for a quick read. High level: we understand the preference for fee alignment. Internal constraints are around our underwriting for large enterprise exposures and precedent for caps tied to fees.

To help focus the conversation, could you confirm:
- Typical annualized spend you expect in year 1 (ballpark is fine)
- Whether Fika would accept a floor (e.g., $500k) if a fee-multiplier approach is used

Markus / Laura — any immediate redlines to flag? If we can get a legal-oriented counter today, I'll take it back to James and suggest a Wednesday call.

Best,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T19:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Liability cap ask — alignment to fees paid (internal)

Internal note / recommended positions (short):

Context: customer asks for (i) greater of $1.5M or 3x fees in prior 12 months; alternate ask is 2x total fees over contract term.

Recommended Redwood stance (options to propose formally):
1) Commercially preferred (fast close): Rolling 12-month cap equal to 1x fees paid, with a contractual floor of $500k and an absolute ceiling of $3M for the initial 12 months. Rationale: ties exposure to spend while limiting runaway exposure.

2) Conservative legal fallback (standard): Aggregate cap equal to 2x fees actually paid under the contract term, no annualization. Rationale: simpler to administer and caps total lifetime exposure.

3) Executive exception (rare): 3x fees (rolling 12 months) only if signed off by Head of Commercial + Legal and subject to additional underwriting (SLA credits, insurance confirmation).

Carveouts we should insist on (non-negotiable):
- IP indemnity, willful misconduct/fraud, and Redwood obligations under data protection laws (including data breach liability) are carved out from the cap (we can limit to direct damages for negligence but not for intentional or statutory liabilities).
- Consequential damages: keep mutual exclusion; customer can request limited consequential carveouts tied to third-party integrations but must be narrowly drafted.

Operational asks for sales/rev ops:
- If we propose an annualized/rolling cap, Rev Ops needs to confirm how fees will be measured (invoice basis? cash receipts?) and whether monthly proration applies for mid-term changes.
- Add a runway for a joint underwriting checklist for deals above $2M annual spend.

I've attached a quick model (internal_liability_model.xlsx) showing exposure scenarios at 0.5x/1x/2x/3x for different spend profiles.

If you want, I can draft two redline snippets (one for 1x rolling + floor, one for 2x aggregate) and we can present both to Fika.

-Markus
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: internal_liability_model.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: James O'Neil <james.oneil@fikahealth.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@fikahealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Liability cap ask — alignment to fees paid

James — thanks for the redlines and for the patient back-and-forth.

Quick commercial counter (to move toward a decision):
- Proposal A (preferred): Liability cap = the greater of (i) $500,000 or (ii) an amount equal to 1x Fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim (rolling 12-month lookback). Absolute ceiling for the first 12 months of the contract = $3,000,000.
- Proposal B (if Fika prefers term simplicity): Aggregate liability cap = 2x Fees actually paid under the Agreement over the entire contract term.

Non-negotiable carveouts: IP indemnity, liabilities arising from willful misconduct/fraud, and damages required by law (including statutory data breach remedies) will be carved out from the cap. Consequential damages remain mutually excluded except for narrowly-defined third-party integration claims (we can scope those in a SOW).

Operational point: we measure Fees on invoiced amounts in Redwood's billing system; Rev Ops will confirm proration for mid-term amendments. If either option is acceptable, Markus can provide redline snippets to slot into the MSA and we can run a short exec approval for Proposal A if Fika requests a higher multiplier.

Next step: can we take 20 minutes on Wednesday (May 14) to confirm which proposal Fika prefers? If you want Proposal A but want to push to 2x instead of 1x, we'll need a short underwriting exercise.
